requirement:
An outline input MUST be rewritten only if the mapped node exists and its
structural hash, computed under
{cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash` over the
{term}`requirements.refactor.mapped_back` text of the node, equals the recorded
hash.
rationale:
The subject has three independent conditions: the mapped node exists, its hash is computed over the mapped-back text, and the hash equals the recorded hash. An outline input is rewritten only when all three hold. I did not read the implementation. I derived the expected behavior from the requirement text and the `requirements.refactor.mapped_back` definition. `requirements.references.structural_hash` is cited context and was not reassessed.

- **Rewrite when the node exists and the hash matches.** `tests/refactor.rs#fn[a_moved_function_keeps_its_evidence_current]` moves `fn[load]` unchanged to a new file. It asserts that `evidence/rules.load.json` changes, that `inputs[1].file` becomes `src/config/load.rs`, and that `errors(root)` is empty afterwards. It also asserts that an unaffected record stays byte-identical and that a second run changes 0 records.
- **No rewrite when the hash differs.** `tests/refactor.rs#fn[a_function_edited_while_moving_leaves_its_records_stale]` edits the function while moving it. It asserts that the report says `inputs[1]: ... no longer has the recorded hash`. It asserts that the record file is byte-identical afterwards, and that validation still reports errors. An implementation that rewrites without checking the hash would fail this test.
- **No rewrite when the mapped node is missing.** `tests/refactor.rs#fn[an_input_whose_node_is_missing_after_the_move_is_not_rewritten]` moves the file without `fn[verify]`. It asserts the report line `no outline node matches "fn[verify]"` and that the record is byte-identical.
- **Hash computed over the mapped-back text.** `tests/refactor.rs#fn[a_rename_rewrites_the_hash_of_a_node_whose_doc_comment_names_it]` renames a requirement that a hashed doc comment names. The node's current text differs from the recorded text, so the hash matches only if it is computed over the mapped-back text. The test asserts that the input is rewritten, that the new hash differs from the old one, and that the recorded hash equals the new one. An implementation that hashed the unmapped current text would leave the record stale and fail this test.
- **Mapped-back text itself.** `src/refactor/tests.rs#fn[mapped_back_text_replaces_whole_new_names_and_paths]` checks the mapped-back substitution for names, paths, and node addresses. It covers whole-name and whole-path boundaries, so longer names and other paths are left alone.

All five tests carry `{test}` references to the subject. I found no unreferenced relevant test, no untested obligation, and no ambiguity.

text: :::{req} outline_inputs
An outline input MUST be rewritten only if the mapped node exists and its
structural hash, computed under
{cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash` over the
{term}`requirements.refactor.mapped_back` text of the node, equals the recorded
hash.
:::{req} structural_hash
A node's structural hash MUST be the SHA-256 digest of an unambiguous encoding of
its outline-relevant structure, including siblings its profile attaches to it:
the kinds of its named grammar nodes and, in source order, its text pieces. A
text piece MUST be the text of a leaf token, or text inside a node that no child
token covers. Each text piece MUST be hashed as its ordered list of words, where
words are separated by whitespace, the whitespace itself, including leading and
trailing whitespace, is never hashed, and each word is encoded separately, so
`ab cd` and `abcd` differ. The same rule MUST apply in every language. Comments
MUST be excluded, except comment kinds the profile includes; the Rust profile MUST include doc comments. For an included comment, only its text and its
profile's comment group MUST be hashed, not its delimiter tokens such as `//`,
`///`, `//!`, `/*`, `*/`, or a leading `*`; the Rust profile's groups are inner
and outer doc comments. The words of consecutive included comments of one group
MUST be hashed as one ordered list, so reflowing them across more or fewer lines
or comments does not change the hash, while moving text between groups does. A `line`
node's hash MUST be computed by the same word rule over the line's text. A node's
identity hash MUST be computed the same way but MUST also exclude its outline
descendants and their attached siblings, so editing a descendant does not change
its ancestors' selectors.
:::{definition} mapped_back
:phrase: mapped-back
The *mapped-back* form of current text or a current address is the text or
address with each new side of the mappings replaced by its old side.
